trivia.title: The city axis made power legible
trivia.body: Beijing's north-south ceremonial axis turns imperial hierarchy into an urban walking experience rather than just a court diagram.

trivia.title: Chang'an once felt larger than memory suggests
trivia.body: Modern Xi'an preserves the capital memory, but the Tang-era Chang'an grid once spread far beyond what many visitors now picture from the old walls alone.

trivia.title: Brocade and irrigation helped the city feel rich
trivia.body: Chengdu's reputation for urban comfort was tied not only to scenery but also to a basin economy that turned irrigation, craft, and transport into everyday abundance.

trivia.title: West Lake was political atmosphere too
trivia.body: In Hangzhou, lake scenery was never only leisure background; it also shaped how the city imagined refined rule, poetry, and capital prestige.

trivia.title: One port could feel more global than the court center
trivia.body: Late imperial Guangzhou exposed local residents to goods, intermediaries, and foreign merchants in ways that could feel more outward-facing than many inland political capitals.
